text:
Arjun V: hey all, excited to be here! quick snag on first-day laptop setup: my MacBook Pro (M1) enrolled via ABM/MDM but I can't enable FileVault and my YubiKey SSH sign-in isn't working. SSH agent reports 'key unavailable' and `ssh-add -l` shows nothing. Also `fdesetup enable` errors with 'User does not have SecureToken'. Anyone seen this?
Tessa (IT): welcome Arjun! congrats and sorry for the bump. Looks like the account provisioned without a SecureToken, which prevents FileVault escrow. Did you sign in at the macOS login screen with the SSO Apple ID or create a local password during setup?
Arjun V: I followed the quickstart and used the corporate Apple ID when prompted, but I think I skipped the extra password step and just created a local account in the assistant. Not sure which step grants SecureToken.
Rico (Eng Manager): welcome again — FYI we want you to enable FileVault and get the YubiKey working for SSH/GitHub so you can push code. Tag us if you need repo access whitelisting.
IT Helpdesk: ticket #INC-94567 opened and assigned to Tessa. Please DM the device serial instead of posting it. :ticket:
mdm-bot: Device serial matched. Enrollment: Completed. Pending actions: grant SecureToken (if required), push yubikey config, escrow FileVault key. Available actions: `push-securetoken-fix`, `grant-ephemeral-admin`, `resend-fde-profile`, `push-ssh-config`.
Tessa (IT): common fix: create a separate admin user temporarily (via a managed one-time admin token) that receives a SecureToken during initial creation, then use sysadminctl to grant the SecureToken to your primary account. Security prefers we avoid creating persistent extra admins. Nina (Security), any constraints?
Nina (Security): short policy: ephemeral admin is allowed for device provisioning. We must audit the token and ensure it auto-expires. No permanent admin or SIP changes. If MDM can push a SecureToken transfer without admin, prefer that.
Arjun V: I'd rather avoid extra accounts if possible. Is there an MDM way to transfer SecureToken?
Tessa (IT): some MDMs can issue a DEP/ABM reconnect that triggers SecureToken assignment when the first admin is created via Setup Assistant, but it's hit-or-miss. We'll try a targeted MDM workflow first: pushing a managed admin creation that comes with SecureToken and then immediately transfer it and revoke admin. I'll push a one-hour admin token if MDM route fails.
Sam (DevEx): FYI for the YubiKey: GitHub SSH signing with a hardware token usually needs a PKCS#11 lib or agent socket. If the keychain isn't allowing the private key, that can be due to key access control entries tied to the login keychain which didn't get unlocked at boot because FileVault wasn't on. Getting SecureToken/FileVault usually fixes the keychain state.
Tessa (IT): mdm-bot: initiating `push-securetoken-fix` for device.
mdm-bot: Action queued -> Creating managed admin account (temporary) -> Delivering -> Installed. Managed admin user created: redwood-admin-temp (expires in 60 minutes). Audit: https://internal.logs/admin-tokens/94567
Arjun V: I see a new user 'redwood-admin-temp' at the login screen. Do I log in to that?
Tessa (IT): yes, log in once and then log out. That account is created to receive a SecureToken. After you log in, we'll run `sysadminctl -adminUser redwood-admin-temp -adminPassword <password> -secureTokenOn arjun -password <yourpassword>` remotely, then revoke the temp admin. We'll DM you the temp password.
Arjun V: logged in as redwood-admin-temp and back to my account.
mdm-bot: Executing remote SecureToken transfer. Command: `sysadminctl -adminUser redwood-admin-temp -adminPassword ******** -secureTokenOn arjun -password ********` -> Success. SecureToken now present on account 'arjun'.
Arjun V: ran `fdesetup enable` and it now prompts to escrow. It asked for my password and finished. FileVault is On. Nice. :tada:
Sam (DevEx): after FileVault is enabled, reboot once to ensure login keychain unlocks at boot and the YubiKey middleware sees the agent. For the YubiKey SSH, we prefer using 'yubikey-agent' with the PKCS#11 slot rather than Apple Keychain. I'll DM you a short install snippet you can run without admin.
Arjun V: quick question — the YubiKey PIN prompt isn't showing at login; I can still unlock with password but not the YubiKey touch. Is that expected?
Tessa (IT): the YubiKey won't replace password at the macOS login screen unless we configure a smartcard login via Enterprise SSO and directory binding. We don't enable smartcard login by default for remote hires. The YubiKey can be used for SSH and web auth (passkeys) though. If you want smartcard login we'll need a security review.
Nina (Security): policy note: smartcard login requires strict lifecycle controls and MDM-managed cert provisioning; we only enable it for 1) executives, or 2) teams with explicit approval. For regular engineers we'll set up SSH/passkeys.
mdm-bot: pushing `push-ssh-config` -> delivered -> installed. Config includes a user-level plist to set up socket forwarding and an approved `yubikey-agent` binary.
Arjun V: got the DM with the `yubikey-agent` steps, installed in user directory and ran `eval $(yubikey-agent -l)` and now `ssh-add -L` shows the pubkey. Touching YubiKey signs as expected. Great.
Tessa (IT): revoking managed admin now. mdm-bot: revoke `redwood-admin-temp` -> removed. Audit recorded.
IT Helpdesk: closing ticket #INC-94567 as resolved. If you notice any keychain oddities after reboot, reopen and tag @Tessa (IT). Welcome aboard! :wave:
